phases.title: Data Analysis and SQL Integration
phases.rationale: This phase focuses on enhancing your SQL skills while integrating data analysis with Python. Given your coursework in Database Systems, this project will help you apply SQL in a practical context, addressing your gap in SQL proficiency. You'll also leverage your existing Python skills to analyze data, which will reinforce your understanding of data manipulation and preprocessing techniques.
phases.outcome: You will be able to write complex SQL queries for data extraction and perform data analysis using Python.
phases.checkpoint: After completing this phase, you will be able to effectively manipulate and query data using SQL and analyze it with Python.

learning_actions.title: Student Performance Analysis with SQL and Python
learning_actions.description: 1. Download the Student Performance dataset from Kaggle. 2. Use MySQL to create a database and import the dataset. 3. Write SQL queries to extract relevant features such as study time, grades, and attendance. 4. Optimize your SQL queries for performance (refer to the SQL Query Optimization Techniques tutorial). 5. Use Python (pandas) to load the SQL query results into a DataFrame. 6. Perform data analysis to find correlations between study time and grades. 7. Visualize your findings using Matplotlib or Seaborn.
learning_actions.rationale: This project builds on your existing SQL knowledge from coursework while integrating Python for data analysis. It addresses your gap in SQL manipulation and enhances your data processing skills with pandas.

learning_actions.title: Deploying a PyTorch Model on AWS
learning_actions.description: 1. Build a simple image classification model using PyTorch (follow the Deep Learning with PyTorch tutorial for guidance). 2. Train the model on a suitable dataset (e.g., CIFAR-10). 3. Create a REST API using Flask to serve the model predictions. 4. Deploy the model on AWS using Elastic Beanstalk (refer to the Deploying Machine Learning Models on AWS tutorial). 5. Test the deployment and ensure the API returns predictions correctly.
learning_actions.rationale: This project will give you practical experience with PyTorch and cloud deployment, addressing two significant gaps in your skill set. It also allows you to apply your Python programming skills in a real-world context.

learning_actions.title: Customer Segmentation Analysis with SQL
learning_actions.description: 1. Start by downloading a public dataset, such as the 'Online Retail' dataset from UCI Machine Learning Repository. 2. Import the dataset into a MySQL database. 3. Write SQL queries to clean the data, including handling missing values and duplicates. 4. Create a customer segmentation model by grouping customers based on their purchase behavior using SQL aggregation functions. 5. Visualize the results using Python libraries like Matplotlib or Seaborn to create plots that show customer segments. 6. Document your SQL queries and findings in a Jupyter Notebook, explaining the logic behind your queries and the insights gained from the analysis.
learning_actions.rationale: This project will help you gain a strong understanding of SQL for data manipulation and querying, which is currently a gap for you. It also allows you to leverage your existing Python skills for data visualization and analysis, reinforcing your proficiency in Python for developing data processing pipelines.

learning_actions.title: Deploying a Machine Learning Model on AWS
learning_actions.description: 1. Build a simple machine learning model using scikit-learn (e.g., a regression model on a dataset of your choice). 2. Prepare the model for deployment by creating a REST API using Flask. 3. Follow a tutorial to deploy your Flask app on AWS using Elastic Beanstalk. 4. Create a simple front-end interface to interact with your model. 5. Use a data visualization library (e.g., Plotly) to create interactive visualizations of the model's predictions. 6. Document the deployment process and visualizations in a Jupyter Notebook.
learning_actions.rationale: This project addresses your gap in familiarity with cloud platforms for deploying machine learning models. It also incorporates data visualization techniques, which you have not yet explored. learning_actions.title: Student Performance Analysis with SQL and Python
learning_actions.description: 1. Download a dataset related to student performance (e.g., student grades). 2. Use MySQL to create a database and import the dataset. 3. Write SQL queries to analyze student performance, focusing on key metrics (e.g., average grades, pass/fail rates). 4. Optimize your SQL queries for performance by applying techniques learned from the provided resources. 5. Use Python (pandas) to load the SQL query results into a DataFrame. 6. Preprocess the data by normalizing and encoding features as necessary. 7. Visualize the results using Matplotlib or Seaborn to present your findings.

Export your trained TensorFlow model to a format suitable for deployment. 3. Use AWS services such as S3 for storage and Elastic Beanstalk or Lambda for deployment. 4. Follow the provided resources to implement cloud deployment strategies for your model. 5. Test the deployed model using a REST API and document the process in a Jupyter Notebook, including code and screenshots of the deployment.
learning_actions.rationale: This project will provide you with hands-on experience in deploying machine learning models on AWS, addressing your gap in cloud platforms. It builds on your previous work with TensorFlow and enhances your overall skill set as a Machine Learning Engineer.

phases.outcome: You will be able to write complex SQL queries to manipulate and visualize data effectively.
phases.checkpoint: After completing this phase, you will be able to perform data manipulation using SQL and visualize findings using Python libraries.

learning_actions.title: Sales Data Analysis and Visualization
learning_actions.description: 1. Download a public sales dataset (e.g., from Kaggle). 2. Use MySQL to create a database and import the dataset. 3. Write SQL queries to perform data cleaning and manipulation, focusing on filtering, aggregating, and joining tables. 4. Export the cleaned data to a CSV file. 5. Use Python (pandas and Matplotlib) to load the CSV and create visualizations (e.g., bar charts, line graphs) to present your findings. 6. Document your process and findings in a Jupyter Notebook.
learning_actions.rationale: This project directly addresses your gap in SQL by requiring you to manipulate and query data effectively. It also introduces data visualization, which you have no prior experience with, using Python libraries you are familiar with.

learning_actions.title: SQL Data Exploration and Visualization
learning_actions.description: 1. Choose a public dataset (e.g., the Titanic dataset) and upload it to a MySQL database. 2. Write SQL queries to explore the dataset, focusing on data cleaning and manipulation (e.g., filtering, aggregating). 3. Document your SQL queries and visualizations in a Jupyter Notebook.

phases.title: Data Preprocessing and Feature Engineering
phases.rationale: This phase focuses on enhancing your understanding of data preprocessing techniques and feature engineering, which are crucial for building effective machine learning models. Given your background in supervised learning and your experience with Python, this phase will help you deepen your skills in these areas while also introducing you to TensorFlow and PyTorch, which are essential frameworks in the industry.

learning_actions.title: Customer Segmentation with K-Means Clustering
learning_actions.description: 1. Download a customer dataset (e.g., from Kaggle). 2. Load the dataset using Pandas and perform initial data exploration (check for missing values, data types, etc.). 3. Preprocess the data by handling missing values and normalizing numerical features. 4. Engineer new features that could help in clustering (e.g., total spending, frequency of purchases). 5. Implement K-Means clustering using scikit-learn and visualize the clusters using Matplotlib. 6. Evaluate the clustering results using silhouette scores and interpret the findings.
learning_actions.rationale: This project builds on your existing skills in Python and scikit-learn while introducing you to data preprocessing and feature engineering techniques. It also allows you to visualize the results, which is a step towards understanding data interpretation.

phases.title: Building Image Classification Models
phases.rationale: This phase focuses on hands-on experience with deep learning frameworks, specifically TensorFlow and PyTorch, which are critical for a Machine Learning Engineer. By building an image classification model, you will learn to preprocess data, implement machine learning algorithms, and evaluate model performance using various metrics. This project will also introduce you to Git for version control, enhancing your collaboration skills.
phases.outcome: You will be able to build and evaluate an image classification model using TensorFlow or PyTorch, demonstrating proficiency in data preprocessing and model evaluation.
phases.checkpoint: After completing this phase, you will be able to build and evaluate an image classification model using TensorFlow or PyTorch.

learning_actions.title: Image Classification with TensorFlow
learning_actions.description: 1. Set up your environment with TensorFlow and Jupyter Notebook. 2. Download the CIFAR-10 dataset from TensorFlow Datasets. 3. Preprocess the data by normalizing pixel values and splitting it into training and testing sets. 4. Build a convolutional neural network (CNN) model using TensorFlow. 5. Train the model on the training set and validate it on the testing set. 6. Evaluate the model's performance using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score metrics. 7. Use Git to version control your project and document your code.
learning_actions.rationale: This project builds on your existing knowledge of machine learning by introducing you to TensorFlow, a key framework for model building. It also incorporates Git for version control, addressing your claimed-only experience with Git.

learning_actions.title: Deploying an Image Classification Model on AWS
learning_actions.description: 1. Complete the AWS setup by creating an account and configuring your environment. 2. Train an image classification model using either TensorFlow or PyTorch (you can use the model from Phase 1). 3. Save the trained model and create a REST API using Flask. 4. learning_actions.title: Image Classification with TensorFlow
learning_actions.description: 1. Set up your environment with TensorFlow and Jupyter Notebook. 2. Download the CIFAR-10 dataset using TensorFlow's built-in functions. 3. Preprocess the data by normalizing pixel values and splitting it into training and testing sets. 4. Build a convolutional neural network (CNN) model using TensorFlow's Keras API. 5. Train the model on the training set and evaluate its performance on the test set using accuracy as a metric. 6. Visualize the training process and model predictions using Matplotlib.
learning_actions.rationale: This project introduces you to TensorFlow, allowing you to apply your Python programming skills in a machine learning context. It also covers model evaluation metrics, addressing your gaps in framework experience and evaluation.

Visualize the results using Matplotlib to create confusion matrices and ROC curves.

learning_actions.title: Housing Price Prediction with TensorFlow
learning_actions.description: 1. Download the Boston Housing dataset from UCI Machine Learning Repository. 2. Use Pandas to load the dataset and perform exploratory data analysis (EDA) to understand the features. 3. Preprocess the data by handling missing values and normalizing the features using MinMaxScaler from scikit-learn. 4. Split the dataset into training and testing sets. 5. Build a neural network model using TensorFlow to predict housing prices based on the features. 6. Train the model and evaluate its performance using Mean Absolute Error (MAE). 7. Visualize the predictions against actual values using Matplotlib.

learning_actions.title: Customer Churn Prediction Model
learning_actions.description: 1. Download the Telco Customer Churn dataset from Kaggle. 2. Use Pandas to load the dataset and examine its structure. 3. Identify and handle missing values using appropriate data cleaning techniques (refer to the tutorial on Data Cleaning Techniques in Python). 4. Perform exploratory data analysis (EDA) to understand the features and their distributions. 5. Preprocess the data by encoding categorical variables and scaling numerical features. 6. Split the dataset into training and testing sets. 7. Build a logistic regression model using scikit-learn to predict customer churn. 8. Evaluate the model's performance using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score (refer to the tutorial on Classification Metrics). 9. Document your findings and visualize the results using Matplotlib.
learning_actions.rationale: This project will help you develop your data preprocessing skills by requiring you to clean and prepare a real-world dataset. learning_actions.title: House Price Prediction with Feature Engineering
learning_actions.description: 1. Download the Ames Housing dataset from Kaggle. 2. Load the dataset using Pandas and perform an initial examination of the data. 3. Identify and clean any missing values and outliers (refer to the Data Cleaning and Preprocessing tutorial). 4. Conduct EDA to identify important features affecting house prices. 5. Create new features based on existing ones (feature engineering). 6. Split the dataset into training and testing sets. 7. Build a decision tree regression model using scikit-learn to predict house prices. 8. Evaluate the model using RMSE and visualize the results. 9. Document your process and findings in a Jupyter Notebook.
learning_actions.rationale: This project will enhance your data preprocessing skills and provide experience with feature engineering, which is crucial for building effective machine learning models. You'll also gain further experience with scikit-learn and model evaluation techniques, addressing multiple gaps simultaneously.

Document your process in a Jupyter Notebook and push your code to a GitHub repository.
learning_actions.rationale: This project builds on your existing Python skills and introduces you to data manipulation using Pandas, which is essential for preprocessing data in machine learning. learning_actions.title: Predictive Model for Housing Prices
learning_actions.description: 1. Gather a dataset on housing prices (e.g., from Kaggle). 2. Use Pandas to load and explore the dataset, checking for missing values and data types. 3. Preprocess the data by handling missing values and normalizing features. 4. Split the dataset into training and testing sets. 5. Implement a supervised learning algorithm (e.g., Linear Regression) using scikit-learn. 6. Evaluate the model using metrics such as RMSE and R-squared. 7. Learn about AWS deployment strategies and deploy your model using AWS SageMaker. 8. Create a simple web interface using Flask to interact with your model.
learning_actions.rationale: This project builds on your existing skills in Python and scikit-learn while introducing you to AWS for deployment. It also emphasizes model evaluation techniques, which you need to strengthen.

learning_actions.title: Image Classification with TensorFlow
learning_actions.description: 1. Set up your environment by installing TensorFlow and necessary libraries. 2. Download the CIFAR-10 dataset, which contains 60,000 32x32 color images in 10 classes. 3. Preprocess the data by normalizing pixel values and splitting it into training and testing sets. 4. Build a simple convolutional neural network (CNN) using TensorFlow's Keras API. 5. Train the model on the training set and evaluate its performance on the test set. 6. Visualize the training process using Matplotlib to plot accuracy and loss over epochs.
learning_actions.rationale: This project builds on your existing Python skills and introduces you to TensorFlow, addressing your gap in machine learning frameworks. It also incorporates data preprocessing techniques, which are crucial for effective model training.

learning_actions.title: Student Performance Prediction Model
learning_actions.description: 1. Use the cleaned dataset from Phase 1. 2. Split the dataset into training and testing sets using scikit-learn. 3. Implement a classification model (e.g., Logistic Regression) to predict student performance. 4. Evaluate the model using metrics such as accuracy, precision, and recall. 5. Use Git to track your code changes and document your process. 6. Visualize the model's performance with Matplotlib, comparing predicted vs actual outcomes.
learning_actions.rationale: This project builds on your experience with scikit-learn from your previous classification model while introducing you to model evaluation metrics and version control. It will solidify your understanding of supervised learning concepts and enhance your coding practices.

learning_actions.description: 1. Download a dataset from Kaggle (e.g., Titanic dataset). 2. Use pandas to load the dataset and examine its structure (shape, dtypes). 3. learning_actions.description: 1. Download the 'House Prices: Advanced Regression Techniques' dataset from Kaggle. 2. Load the dataset using pandas and perform initial data exploration. 3. Document your process and results in a Jupyter Notebook, including visualizations of the model's predictions versus actual prices.
